text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.3 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
This is a public goods game where contributing is individually costly but collectively beneficial—keeping tokens yields 1 to self versus 0.3 to self plus spillover if contributed, so the dominant strategy is to free-ride while full cooperation maximizes group payoff. Since this repeats over 10 rounds with unknown partners, I need to settle on a reasonable contribution level balancing self-interest and cooperation.

I'll go with a moderate starting contribution, around 10 tokens, to signal willingness to cooperate while testing how others respond before committing further.
